title: Form Energy
summary: Massachusetts company commercialising iron-air batteries for hundred-hour grid storage.
bodyHtml:
Form Energy's iron-air battery stores energy through reversible rusting, using iron, water and air instead of lithium. The target is multi-day storage that complements lithium-ion, which is economic for a few hours.

Its first commercial project is with a utility in Minnesota, and the company is building manufacturing capacity in West Virginia.

Why it matters

  • Iron-air chemistry
  • 100-hour duration target
  • Utility-scale projects

businessMeaning: The grid needs duration more than it needs more two-hour batteries. Iron is cheap and abundant, but round-trip efficiency is lower than lithium.
investmentLens: Private; a long-duration storage bet whose success would pressure gas peakers more than lithium suppliers.
